claims.claim: eel, white sucker, brown bullhead, yellow perch and sticklebacks all refused perch ribbons in feeding trials (Newsome & Tompkins 1985, abstract)
claims.note: full text not obtained. The abstract (not used to confirm) says no egg masses were consumed when offered to eel, white sucker, brown bullhead, yellow perch, and three- and nine-spined sticklebacks, although alternative foods were often eaten; that eel and white sucker caught on perch spawning sites at the peak had none in their stomachs; and that hatchery brook trout ate egg masses without harm, suggesting an unpalatable rather than toxic substance. The paper's sentence matches the abstract; the numbers of fish and trials, and whether ribbons were offered whole, need the full text

claims.claim: predation on perch ribbons over the egg stage ~0 (Newsome & Tompkins 1985)
claims.note: as above. By the abstract, the evidence is refusal in trials and empty stomachs at spawning sites for two species; it does not measure field predation on ribbons by the lakes' other egg eaters (crayfish, snails, pumpkinseed, bass were not among the species the abstract lists). The brook trout result shows a nonselective fish will eat them, so '~0' is an inference beyond the abstract
